correctness.rationale: Center the quadratic probe response as X=sum_{i<j} B_ij Z_iZ_j. Any scalar self-coupling of X lifts to uniform full-vector probe marginals by independently sampling within level-set fibers; antitone quantile pairing minimizes covariance by rearrangement. For n<=3 the antipodal quotient has at most 4 classes, and every perfect matching on 4 is a translation by a fixed coordinate sign pattern, including ties. For K_n, X=((sum Z_i)^2-n)/2 and sorted binomial multiplicities give exact minimum. Balanced flip has variance 4(C(n,2)-floor(n²/4)). Source supplies a strict comonotone-pair swap for all n>=4, and CLT plus second-moment/W2 convergence validates the reflected quantile limit. Independent enumeration verified exact antitone and flip variances for every K_n with 4<=n<=12 (K4: 6 vs 8; independent 12). Decimal limit is not certified.
residual_risks: Optimal coupling may require the whole scalar response law and may not be efficient in matrix-free black-box computations.
Small finite checks are corroboration, not the proof for all n; the asymptotic decimal is approximate.

value.rationale: Optimizing two Hutchinson/Rademacher sign probes under fixed correct marginals is a natural variance frontier. The theorem quantifies the first sharp dimension where an easily implemented sign-flip dependence is suboptimal, gives an unweighted K4 witness and a complete all-n family plus limit. It is an exact structural benchmark even though the optimal nonlocal coupling need not yield a practical fast trace algorithm.
residual_risks: This is not a claimed new optimal transport theorem or efficient end-to-end algorithm.

final_claim: For every real symmetric n<=3 matrix, fixed coordinate sign flips attain optimal coupling variance for two full-uniform Rademacher trace probes; for complete-graph adjacency matrices K_n, n>=4, unrestricted nonlinear dependence strictly improves every flip with exact sorted-binomial optimum, K4 variances 12/8/6 and reflected-chi-square limiting ratio about 0.5606716.
limitations: Two full-uniform Rademacher marginals and a fixed known real symmetric matrix; no general trace algorithm optimality.
The asymptotic numerical ratio is approximate; its exact mathematical statement is an integral.
